motivo: Todas las afirmaciones de salud/seguridad y cifras quedaron verificadas con fuentes de EE. UU. (CDC, USDA FSIS, NC State/J Food Prot). Unidades y cifras coinciden (165 °F, 60% = 'six in ten', ~300 personas). No hay afirmaciones probables, dudosas ni falsas. Observaciones menores no bloqueantes: (1) el 60% proviene del reporte FSIS 2019 (la caption lo cita bien); el campo 'fuentes' del guion lo asocia al paper J Food Prot 2022, que es la publicacion del mismo estudio, sin efecto en el texto hablado. (2) La pagina CDC de pollo dice 'no hace falta lavarlo' y la de prevencion agrega 'puede esparcir germenes a otros alimentos, el fregadero y la mesada'; ambas respaldan la frase.

afirmaciones.texto: You rinse your raw chicken before cooking it. (premisa del gancho, practica comun, no es afirmacion factica sobre el mundo)
afirmaciones.fuente: n/a (gancho retorico; USDA/NC State: 61% del grupo control lavaba el pollo)

afirmaciones.texto: That's backwards. / Skip the rinse, cook it, done. (recomendacion: no lavar el pollo crudo)
afirmaciones.fuente: CDC https://www.cdc.gov/food-safety/foods/chicken.html ('Raw chicken is ready to cook. It doesn't need to be washed first'); USDA FSIS 'Washing Raw Poultry: Our Science, Your Choice' (usda.gov/article/washing-raw-poultry-our-science-your-choice)

afirmaciones.texto: Water doesn't kill the bacteria. It can just spread them.
afirmaciones.fuente: USDA FSIS (agosto 2019): lavar/enjuagar carne y aves no destruye bacterias; CDC https://www.cdc.gov/food-safety/prevention/index.html (puede esparcir germenes). 'can' esta bien como matiz.

afirmaciones.texto: The CDC says rinsing can spread germs to your sink, your counter, and other food.
afirmaciones.fuente: CDC, Preventing Food Poisoning https://www.cdc.gov/food-safety/prevention/index.html: 'Washing these foods can spread germs to other foods, the sink, and the counter'; tambien https://www.cdc.gov/food-safety/communication-resources/washing-chicken-spreads-germs.html

afirmaciones.texto: A USDA-backed study put about three hundred people in test kitchens.
afirmaciones.fuente: USDA FSIS / NC State, 300 participantes (158 control, 142 tratamiento) en cocinas de prueba; J Food Prot 2022 (Foodsafetynews 2022/04; ScienceDaily 2022-04-04). 'about' correcto.

afirmaciones.texto: Of those who washed their chicken, six in ten had bacteria in the sink afterward.
afirmaciones.fuente: USDA FSIS, comunicado 20 ago 2019 (usda.gov/article/washing-raw-poultry-our-science-your-choice): 'Of the participants who washed their raw poultry, 60 percent had bacteria in their sink after washing or rinsing'. 60% = six in ten.

afirmaciones.texto: Cooking is what kills them: chicken needs to hit one hundred sixty-five degrees inside. (caption: 165°F)
afirmaciones.fuente: CDC https://www.cdc.gov/food-safety/foods/chicken.html: 'safe internal temperature of 165°F'; USDA FSIS. Unidad °F coincide (el guion dice 'degrees', publico de EE. UU.).

afirmaciones.texto: Wash your hands with soap and water after touching raw chicken.
afirmaciones.fuente: CDC https://www.cdc.gov/food-safety/foods/chicken.html: 'Wash hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds before and after handling raw chicken'

afirmaciones.texto: Caption: 'In a USDA-backed study with about 300 people in test kitchens, 60% of those who washed their chicken had bacteria in the sink afterward.' y 'Sources: CDC; USDA FSIS chicken-washing study (2019 report); Journal of Food Protection, 2022.'
afirmaciones.fuente: USDA FSIS 2019 (60%, ~300 participantes, NC State) y J Food Prot 2022 (publicacion del estudio). Atribucion correcta.

afirmaciones.texto: Caption: 'Water doesn't kill the bacteria on chicken, and the CDC says rinsing can spread germs to your sink, your counter, and other food.'

afirmaciones.fuente: n/a: dato interno de la cuenta, no afirmacion factica externa
